subtopics.name: Key points
points: Three domains: Bacteria, Archaea, Eukarya (based on 16S rRNA).
Five kingdoms: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia (Whittaker, 1969).
Taxonomic hierarchy: 8 ranks from Domain to Species.
Binomial nomenclature: Genus species (italicised, two-part Latin name).
Alternation of generations: key feature of all land plants.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Binomial nomenclature: Genus + specific epithet (e.g., Homo sapiens)
Alternation of generations: Sporophyte (2n) → Spores (n) → Gametophyte (n) → Gametes → Zygote (2n)

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: The three-domain system reorganised all life into three primary lineages based on 16S rRNA sequence analysis.
Whittaker's five-kingdom system remains the most widely used classification in school-level biology.
All land plants undergo alternation of generations between haploid and diploid phases.

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: Very frequent: tabulate the five kingdoms (cell type, nutrition, examples).
Explain three-domain system with 16S rRNA evidence.
Draw and label the taxonomic hierarchy.
5 kingdoms: M-P-F-P-A (Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia).
3 domains: B-A-E (Bacteria, Archaea, Eukarya).

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Fungi are eukaryotic, heterotrophic, chitin cell wall, no chloroplasts.
Four groups: Phycomycetes, Ascomycetes, Basidiomycetes, Deuteromycetes.
Body = mycelium (hyphae); reproduction = asexual (spores/budding) + sexual.
Ascomycetes → asci; Basidiomycetes → basidia.
Economic roles: decomposers, food, medicine, industry; harmful: diseases, crop blights.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Fungal cell wall: chitin (N-acetylglucosamine polymer)
Yeast budding: mother cell → bud → daughter cell (asexual)
Ascomycete spore: ascus (sac) containing ascospores (8 typically)
Basidiomycete spore: basidium (club) bearing basidiospores (4 typically)

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: Fungi are the primary decomposers in most ecosystems, recycling organic matter.
The chitin cell wall distinguishes fungi from plants (cellulose) and animals (no wall).
Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes are the two most evolutionarily advanced fungal groups.

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: Draw and label Penicillium (conidiophore, conidia, sterigmata) — very common.
Tabulate four fungal groups (spore, example, use).
Explain why fungi are not plants.
Fungi = F-H-C (Heterotrophic, Chitin wall) — remember "Fungi Hates Cellulose".
Asco = sac; Basidio = club; Deutero = imperfect.

subtopics.name: Common misconceptions
points: Fungi have a chitin cell wall (like arthropods), NOT cellulose (like plants).
Fungi are NOT plants: they are heterotrophic, lack chlorophyll, and are in a separate kingdom.
Deuteromycetes are "imperfect" fungi — they have lost the sexual stage; they are not a true phylogenetic…

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Algae are photosynthetic, mostly aquatic, lack true vascular tissues.
Three major groups: Chrysophyceae, Pyrrophyceae, Chlorophyceae.
Ecological role: ~50% of Earth's O₂; base of aquatic food chains.
Reproduction: asexual (spores, fragmentation) + sexual (isogamy, anisogamy, oogamy).
Economic uses: food, industry (agar, alginates), biofertilisers.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Green algae: Chlorophyll a + b, store starch
Brown algae: Chlorophyll a + c + fucoxanthin, store laminarin
Red algae: Chlorophyll a + d + phycobilins, store floridean starch
Diatom cell wall: SiO₂ (silica)

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: Algae are the primary producers of most aquatic ecosystems.
They contribute approximately 50% of global oxygen via photosynthesis.
Diatoms have silica cell walls and form the base of the marine food web.

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: Tabulate algal groups (pigment, storage, example, reproduction).
Explain the ecological importance of algae (5 points).
Describe algal blooms and their environmental impact.
Algae = A-O-A (Aquatic, Oxygen, Aquatic food base).
Green algae = starch; Brown = laminarin; Red = floridean starch.
